A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPO research. The main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original TigerDoor, Brax and POPGym experiments, ablations, learning curves and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds RMA results and further GPO-clip comparisons in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Equation (10) corrects the stated backtracking mask from pi(a|s)/mu(a|o) to mu(a|s)/pi(a|o), changing its formal activation condition. The four-step framework, architecture and GPO variants remain. The objective-to-loss sign conversions do not establish a different implemented training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same TigerDoor problems, 28 Brax task/noise settings and 15 POPGym tasks. The added comparisons use existing Brax environments; no additional task or observation scenario is established.

E2.justification: v2 adds RMA as an evaluated representation-learning comparator in Appendix E.4 and Figure 11. TGRL, L2T-PPO and the main-text baselines already appeared in v1 and remain.

E3.justification: New Figure 14 introduces a joint-versus-separated update control for GPO-clip on five existing Brax tasks, and Figure 15 evaluates guider and learner rewards separately. The original hyperparameters, preprocessing and training budgets in Tables 5–8 remain unchanged; the new update control receives little procedural explanation.

E4.justification: Figures 14–15 add diagnostics concerning update coupling and guider–learner performance alignment. These supplement the retained supervision ablations, threshold sensitivity studies and shared-versus-separated network analysis in Figure 13.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 newly specifies 10 random seeds for Brax, three for POPGym, and mean and standard deviation reporting for reward curves. v1 already displayed shaded curves without this explanation. The disclosure does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Figure 11 adds RMA learning curves across the existing 28 Brax settings. Figures 14–15 add results showing, for example, higher rewards from joint updates on HumanoidStandup and generally similar guider and learner rewards. The main benchmark figures and Table 9 timing values are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the backtracking mask in Equation (10) changes its policy ratio, a localized correction beyond equivalent notation. Propositions 1–2, their proofs in Appendix B and the TigerDoor-alt derivation in Appendix D remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: aligned guider–learner co-training, learner optimality comparable to direct RL, and strong performance on noisy control and memory tasks. The additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly clarifies that optimality concerns the partially observable learner. It also adds decodability qualifications for reconstruction approaches and attributes RMA's difficulties under noise to limitations of latent reconstruction. The existing GPO failure conditions and parameter-sharing tradeoff remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds reproducibility information through the disclosed run counts. Hyperparameter tables, codebase references, preprocessing and hardware reporting remain. However, rewriting Equations (11)–(12) as losses while retaining Algorithm 1's instruction to maximize them introduces an implementation ambiguity.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 and Appendix A add positioning against privileged-information reconstruction, citing Cai, Efroni, Kumar, Qi, Seo and Sermanet and colleagues. This extends the existing discussion without replacing its main framing around imitation, co-training and asymmetric RL.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted introductory and background rewrites, clarifies terminology, shortens the GPS explanation and removes duplicated TGRL discussion. It also updates affiliations and adds acknowledgments and an LLM-use disclosure. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain.

P2.justification: The document adopts conference formatting throughout, with redesigned front matter, headings, headers and bibliography. Figures 1–2 are enlarged, the payoff tables move from the experiments to the background, and appendix displays are rearranged. Figure 11 gains RMA curves and Figures 14–15 are added; most existing plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves empirical transparency through explicit seed and uncertainty reporting, an additional comparator and targeted GPO-clip diagnostics. Clarifying learner-relative optimality also improves interpretation. These gains are limited by sparse implementation details for the new comparisons and the introduced conflict between loss signs and Algorithm 1's maximization instruction; the central results and proofs remain unchanged.
